title: Min Stack
spaceBreakdown:
- vector<int> data: up to n entries → O(n)  
- vector<int> mins: up to n entries → O(n)  
- recursion depth: none  
- not counted: input, returned values
approach: Maintain two parallel stacks. The first stores every pushed value. The second stores, at each depth, the minimum of all elements up to that depth. When pushing, the new minimum is either the new value or the previous minimum; when popping, both stacks shrink together, so the current minimum is always at the top of the second stack. This gives O(1) time for every operation.
hints:
After pushing a new element, how does the overall minimum of the stack change?  
There are at most 3·10⁴ method calls.

Use two stacks: one for the raw values, one that keeps the minimum seen so far.  
Example from the statement: after pushing -2, 0, -3 the top of the “min” stack is -3.

push(x):
    push x onto valueStack
    if minStack empty or x ≤ top(minStack) then push x onto minStack
    else push top(minStack) onto minStack
pop():
    pop valueStack
    pop minStack
top(): return top(valueStack)
getMin(): return top(minStack)

**Single element** - only one value ever exists in the stack.  
`Input: ["MinStack","push","getMin","pop","push","getMin"]` → `Expected: [null,null,5,null,null,5]`  
⚠️ Bug: keeping a single variable min and not updating it on pop → after pop, min still 5 → returns 5 incorrectly.

**Duplicate minima** - several equal minimum values are present.  
`Input: ["MinStack","push","push","push","getMin","pop","getMin","pop","getMin"]` with pushes 2, 2, 2 → `Expected: [null,null,null,null,2,null,2,null,2]`  
⚠️ Bug: updating min only when the new value is < current min → after popping one 2, min remains unchanged → still correct, but fails when the popped value was the only occurrence of the minimum.

**Decreasing sequence** - each new element is smaller than the previous one.  
`Input: ["MinStack","push","push","push","getMin","pop","getMin","pop","getMin"]` with pushes -1, -2, -3 → `Expected: [null,null,null,null,-3,null,-2,null,-1]`  
⚠️ Bug: storing only the global minimum without a stack → after popping -3, min remains -3 instead of -2.

**Extreme negative** - values near INT_MIN.  
`Input: ["MinStack","push","push","getMin"]` with pushes -2147483648, 0 → `Expected: [null,null,null,-2147483648]`  
⚠️ Bug: computing new minimum as a+b or using overflow‑prone arithmetic → may wrap around and give a positive number.

followUps.q: How would you achieve getMin in O(1) time while using only O(1) extra space?
followUps.a: Encode the previous minimum inside the stored value when a new element becomes the new minimum (e.g., store 2*val‑prevMin). Decoding on pop restores the old minimum. All operations stay O(1) and only one stack is needed.

followUps.q: Suppose you also need to support getMax in O(1) time.
followUps.a: Keep a third stack that tracks the maximum in the same way as the minimum stack, pushing the larger of the new value and the previous maximum. All four operations remain O(1) with O(n) space.

followUps.q: What if the stack must handle up to 10⁹ operations but you can only store O(1) elements at any moment (streaming scenario)?
followUps.a: You cannot answer getMin exactly without storing the whole history; you would need an approximate or probabilistic structure (e.g., a min‑heap with limited size) or relax the requirement to “return the minimum seen so far” using a single variable that updates on push but cannot be restored after a pop.
